caption:
Type one sentence. Your browser rewrites the website for you.

Sider Code shipped inside the Sider browser extension on September 1st, and it does something that still sounds like fiction: you describe how you wish a page worked, in plain English, and it rewrites that page's actual code, live, right in your browser.

No developer tools, no coding, no digging through GitHub for someone else's userscript, no installing five different single-purpose extensions and hoping they don't conflict with each other.

Here's what people are already doing with it: turning a 400-comment Reddit thread into a readable overview of the actual debate. Collapsing a scattered X thread into one clean article with its own table of contents. Telling a too-bright, cluttered site to calm down into a dark, quiet workspace. Deleting the YouTube Shorts shelf, permanently — the fix saves itself and reapplies automatically every time you go back.

One honest catch: the code it writes is frozen the moment you apply it. If a site redesigns later, your customization can quietly break, and Sider hasn't shipped a way to detect that yet — it's on their roadmap. Think of this as delightfully hacky and personal, not a permanent fix.

Still strange to think this used to take five extensions and a GitHub search, and now it's a text box.

Save this so you remember to try it on the one site that's been annoying you for years. Full breakdown — link in bio.
